::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 2nd [1862]  
**From:** Otterbourne/ Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1862/ 7
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)

I am sorry my counsels only led to disappointment but I daresay it is wise in poor old [Mr Parker](people/person_1144.qmd) to undertake as little as possible. I should think you were in good hands with [Bell & Daldy](organizations/other_135.qmd). I know [Mrs Gatty](people/person_549.qmd) thinks them very liberal. In one case I knew where a lady wanted to publish a story rather longer than yours, they offered to take it if she would guarantee £30 in case the book failed- she did not like to do this, so it went off, but I think that would be a good course with your story.

I think they are attentive and courteous to their clients, twice they have sent on people to me when they thought a thing better for the [M P](organizations/other_52.qmd) than for themselves one was the [Xmas story](other_books/otherbook_340.qmd) in this number the other [Little Maggie](other_books/otherbook_339.qmd) which I did not like, but they printed

So Rose & are some shades less naughty, I cannot guess in what form her chastisement will come, I begin to hope you won’t kill Rosemary as I dreaded

yours sincerely

C M Yonge

---

**Note:** Envelope addressed to Miss Smith/ 8 Wellington Road/ Old Charlton/ SE and postmarked Winchester 2 December 1862 and London SE 3 December 1862. The envelope also enclosing a letter from John William Parker, Sr., dated 19 November 1862.
